title: Disney+ and Hulu raise prices by up to 13 percent after doubling profits
gist: Disney raised Disney+ and Hulu prices (ad-free standalone plans up 13% to $21.50/month) and several ESPN bundles, its fourth Disney+ hike in four years, right after Disney+ and Hulu operating income jumped 116% YoY to $712 million. The pricing now sits above Netflix's non-4K tiers and appears designed to push subscribers into stickier bundles.

insights.claim: Disney+ and Hulu standalone ad-free plans rose 13% from $19 to $21.50 per month, while standalone ad-supported plans rose only from $12 to $12.50, widening the premium-vs-ads price gap.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Steeper hikes on ad-free tiers nudge users toward ad tiers, growing Disney's ad inventory; watch ad-tier mix in Disney's next earnings.
insights.locator: Disney+ and Hulu’s respective standalone, ad-free plans

insights.claim: Disney raised ESPN-inclusive bundle prices: Disney+/Hulu/ESPN Select with ads went from $20 to $22 and without ads from $29 to $33, while the Disney+/Hulu ad-free bundle rose from $20 to $22 and the $13 ad-supported Disney+/Hulu bundle was left unchanged.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Holding the cheapest ad bundle flat while raising standalone prices makes bundles relatively more attractive, supporting ARPU and retention.
insights.locator: However, prices increased for the Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN Select bundles

insights.claim: Hulu + Live TV, Disney's internet-delivered cable-channel package, went up by $10 per month, following an increase to both ESPN streaming tiers on September 17.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Disney is raising prices across its entire streaming portfolio in one window, signaling confidence in pricing power across live TV and sports.
insights.locator: Monthly subscription prices for Hulu + Live

insights.claim: The September 2026 Disney+ increase is described as its fourth price hike in four years, following hikes in December 2022, October 2023, October 2024, and October 2025, while Hulu raised prices every October from 2022 through 2025, making annual fall price increases a predictable pattern.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Annual fall hikes are effectively a recurring ARPU lever; model them into Disney DTC revenue forecasts.
insights.quote: Disney+ got its fourth price hike in four years today.
insights.locator: The last time that Disney+ raised prices

insights.claim: After the hike, Disney+ and Hulu ad-free plans ($21.50) are more expensive than Netflix's standard ad-free plan ($20) and far above Netflix's $9 ad tier, undercut only by Netflix's $27 4K premium plan.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Disney is pricing above the category leader despite far fewer subscribers, a test of churn tolerance worth watching in subscriber numbers.
insights.quote: That means Disney+ and Hulu are both more expensive than the most popular streaming service now, unless you want 4K or HDR.

insights.claim: Netflix's most recent quarterly operating income was $4.19 billion, nearly six times the $712 million from Disney+ and Hulu combined, and Netflix had 325 million subscribers versus 131.6 million for Disney+ and 59.7 million for Hulu's on-demand service.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: The profit gap shows how much margin headroom Disney's streaming unit could still capture if it approaches Netflix-like scale economics.
insights.locator: In its most recent quarterly earnings report

insights.claim: The author argues Netflix's success shows there is still ample room for Disney to grow streaming profitability, implying further price increases are plausible.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Netflix serves as the profitability ceiling benchmark for Disney DTC; expect continued margin expansion efforts.
insights.quote: Netflix’s success shows there is still ample room for growth.
insights.locator: Price hikes are likely part of Disney’s ongoing effort

insights.claim: Disney's most recent quarter showed Disney+ and Hulu revenue up 11% and combined operating income up 116% year over year to $712 million, so the new price hikes come on top of already-doubling profits.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Price hikes layered on strong operating leverage could drive further DTC margin expansion in upcoming quarters.
insights.locator: In its most recent quarterly earnings report

insights.claim: Disney's new pricing likely aims to steer customers toward bundles, which streaming providers believe reduce cancellations and help Disney manage the unpredictable advertising market.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Bundle mix is a key churn and ad-volatility hedge; track bundle adoption and churn disclosures.
insights.quote: The new prices may also steer customers more toward bundles, which streaming service providers believe lead to fewer cancellations and help Disney manage the unpredictable ads market.
insights.locator: Price hikes are likely part of Disney’s ongoing effort
